scope: structured Feishu CLI access, controlled system Node enablement, and Tongxin read-only access

problem.summary: Feishu/Lark CLI setup and follow-up reads/writes could be blocked by EcoreX tool security when Node/npm were only available from the host PATH or when non-interactive permission confirmation was unavailable.
userImpact: Users could see Feishu Node enablement blocked even though Node/npm were installed locally.
Feishu CLI follow-up read/write/auth/config actions could require permission confirmation or fail in read-only/non-interactive Web runtimes.
Tongxin read-only access needed to stay open for normal users without opening Tongxin write operations.

changes: Feishu CLI now supports a controlled allow_system_node mode that only adds detected Node/npm/npx directories to the feishu_cli environment.
Feishu CLI clears dangerous inherited Node launch variables before invoking Node/npm/npx.
System Node/npm/npx can be used as external executables only when they come from the recorded system Node directories and the command executable is node/npm/npx.
System/global lark-cli is still not accepted; the actual lark-cli command must resolve inside EcoreX runtime or EcoreX state.
Default config, config-template, desktop sidecar defaults, local WebUI installers, and Linux service installer now enable tools.feishu_cli.allow_system_node.
Permission broker now allows structured feishu_cli status/diagnose/ensure/install/agent_auth/config_init/auth_login/run actions by default, including follow-up read/write CLI calls.
Tongxin CLI remains default read-only; Tongxin read-only actions are allowed and mutating Tongxin commands remain blocked.
Tongxin bootstrap now defaults to EcoreX state tools/tongxin instead of runtime tools/tongxin so user-installed xin_agent_cli.py survives runtime updates.
Local WebUI and Linux service installer configs now point Tongxin bootstrap_dir to writable EcoreX state directories.
preservedContracts: Raw bash/system shell execution is not opened.
System PATH is not globally inherited by EcoreX tools.
System Node access is limited to feishu_cli and to node/npm/npx executables.
Global system lark-cli remains rejected; lark-cli must live in EcoreX runtime/state.
Tongxin remains read-only and still validates commands before subprocess execution.
Feishu CLI output redaction and bounded timeouts remain in place.
